transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-26
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Meyers (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Catalyst Head of ML), Alicia Gomez (SRE Lead), Tom Baker (CTO)

Summary:
Weekly pilot sync to review throughput runs from last 48 hours. Focus on continuous batching behavior, concurrency targets, queueing/backpressure, and KV cache prefixing. Discussed spikes in p95/p99, cost tradeoffs, and next-step test matrix. Action items assigned.

Topics:
- recent steady-state run (12:00-14:00 UTC) results
- continuous batching metrics and how it behaves under bursty traffic
- ideal concurrency target for Catalyst's request mix
- queueing thresholds and backpressure tuning
- KV cache / prefix caching to reduce token compute
- next tests and pricing follow-up

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan: ok, hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we'll give folks a few seconds in case they pop in. this is our weekly checkpoint for the catalyst pilot, specific to throughput and queueing. priya and i will walk through the runs and then open it up.
[00:18] Samir: yep, thanks jordan. we got the run report, skimmed it. had a couple of questions on the p99 spikes we saw around 13:05.
[00:25] Priya: right, so quick context — we ran from 12:00 to 14:00 UTC with the traffic mix you provided, 70% short prompts (<=64 tokens), 30% medium (65-256). concurrency cap was 400, with continuous batching enabled and kv cache at default TTL.
[00:43] Alicia: quick clar — when you say continuous batching, what batching window are you using? i thought that was your adaptive micro-batching?
[00:50] Priya: yeah, it's the continuous batching path — basically adaptive windowing set to 8ms target flush with a max 64-request coalescing. we tuned for latency so it tries to flush quickly but holds for micro-batches. that's why you see good average but occasional p99 bumps when a large request arrives and gets coalesced.
[01:12] Tom: okay makes sense. the spike at 13:05 — was that correlated with an injected burst or something from our side?
[01:18] Priya: i checked logs — there was a short burst of ~800 requests over 20s coming from one of the test runners. the queue depth grew and the runtime widened the batch sizes; p95 stayed ok but p99 went up because of a few long tails.
[01:33] Samir: hmm, that burst shouldn't happen in prod, but it's good to know system behavior. we're trying to figure acceptable p99 tradeoff vs cost.
[01:40] Jordan: right and that's the classic latency vs cost trade. you can lower p99 by lowering concurrency (more workers) or tightening batching flush so fewer big coalesced requests, but that raises per-token cost.
[01:52] Alicia: another question — how deterministic is the kv cache hit rate? our prompts have a lot of common prefixes but with small personalization tokens at the end.
[01:59] Priya: so KV cache helps mostly on shared prefixes, we noticed a ~22% token-reduction for your short prompts with default prefixing. if you enable explicit prefix caching (we flagged 'prefix keys' in the config) you can push that to ~35% for very repetitive prefixes. though misaligned tokenization can reduce benefit — sometimes the transcriber spelled it as K-V cash in places, heh.
[02:25] Samir: ha, yeah. can you give a specific example?
[02:28] Priya: sure — your support-summary prompt often starts with the same 40 tokens. by caching KV states for that prefix, subsequent calls skip early attention computation. we'll share a small script to analyze prefix frequency.
[02:40] Jordan: on the concurrency target — during pilot we used 400 but we've discussed bumping to 600 for the next run to test steady-state. any concerns on your infra side?
[02:48] Alicia: main concern is worker pool limits in our test cluster; we need to ensure we can spin up the extra clients. memory isn't huge but we might see queueing cost. we'll coordinate with infra.
[02:59] Samir: from ML team perspective we'd like to validate 600-concurrency steady-state for 2 hours to ensure p50/p95/p99 look good and cost is tolerable.
[03:09] Priya: great, we'll plan that. couple of tuning knobs we proposed: raise concurrency target to 600, enable prefix caching, tweak the adaptive flush down to 6ms target for lower coalescing, and set queue high-water to 5s (after which backpressure / 429s start).
[03:26] Tom: if you tighten flush to 6ms won't that increase request count and thus cost?
[03:31] Priya: yes, the smaller micro-batches reduce latency but you send more smaller batches, which increases GPU kernel invocation overhead. but with prefix caching it might net-neutral or even reduce cost because fewer tokens are computed. it's workload dependent.
[03:45] Jordan: there's also the option of burst capacity — for expected bursts we can route to a slightly cheaper model variant or to a reserved burst pool. that buys you p99 containment without permanently paying for larger capacity.
[03:57] Samir: curious — do you have data on fallback latency when switching to variant? we worry about correctness differences across variants.
[04:05] Priya: yes we ran a micro-benchmark — switching to a quantized variant added ~30-50ms median and sometimes wider tails; for non-critical short responses it's fine, but for your longer reasoning flows maybe less ideal. we can run a canary for you.
[04:20] Alicia: anything on TLS / encryption overhead? we enable strict TLS and internal KMS — could that add latency?
[04:27] Priya: negligible in our tests; network hops and serialization tend to dominate. if you enable per-token tracing or debug, that can impact latency.
[04:36] Jordan: ok practical plan for the next run: Priya executes a 2-hour run at 600 concurrency with prefix caching on and adaptive flush 6ms. Alicia to ensure client pool can sustain 600 concurrent. Samir to provide the 5 canonical prompts and the realistic traffic mix so we mirror production.
[04:56] Samir: i'll get the prompts and a replay of the last week's traffic by monday.
[05:01] Tom: also on cost — jordan, you mentioned a pricing call?
[05:04] Jordan: yes i'll send an updated pricing sheet with burst, reserved, and private options. for pilots we can extend the pilot credits to cover the next runs.
[05:14] Alicia: one more — queueing thresholds: can you explain the queue high-water behavior again? we want to avoid long latencies and prevent cascading failures.
[05:21] Priya: of course — queue high-water means the request queue depth or wait time threshold that, when exceeded, flips to backpressure mode. we set a conservative default (5s) that will start returning 429s or routing to fallback depending on policy. we can configure graceful drain or immediate reject. for your use-case i'd prefer graceful drain plus fallback to a cheaper variant after 7s.
[05:44] Samir: sounds good. for the SLAs we want p95 < 400ms and p99 < 1200ms for short prompts — is that achievable?
[05:54] Priya: with prefix caching and 600 concurrency i think p95 < 300ms is realistic; p99 hitting 1200ms depends on tail events but yes that's achievable with burst pools and tighter batching.
[06:10] Jordan: quick note — we saw one oddity where a single client produced a large number of long requests that skewed the p99; recommend isolating noisy clients in the replay.
[06:20] Samir: yep we'll filter those.
[06:23] Priya: also small transcription note — some words in our logs turned up weirdly, like 'quanta' got transcribed as 'kwanta' so ignore those in the report.
[06:33] Jordan: alright any blockers on scheduling the next run?
[06:36] Alicia: infra will do the client pool change, but i need a heads-up 24h prior to the test so we can coordinate other jobs.
[06:43] Samir: fair. we'll do monday morning for the run.
[06:46] Jordan: perfect. we'll also include a short checklist: 1) Priya run 2h steady-state at 600; 2) enable prefix caching; 3) adjust flush to 6ms; 4) set queue high-water to 5s and fallback after 7s; 5) Samir to supply prompts and traffic mix.
[07:05] Tom: can you also include a CSV of per-second throughput and latency so we can plug into our dashboards?
[07:11] Priya: yes i'll export per-second metrics and p50/p95/p99 histograms and upload to the shared drive.
[07:16] Jordan: and i'll update the pacing doc and send pricing.
[07:20] Samir: good. last tiny ask — can you show us the KV cache hit map visualization next call?
[07:25] Priya: absolutely, i'll prepare a short visualization that shows prefix frequency and potential token savings.
[07:31] Jordan: cool. anything else from catalyst side?
[07:34] Alicia: nope that's it.
[07:36] Tom: all good. thanks.
[07:38] Jordan: thanks everyone. recap and i'll follow up with the sheet and the calendar invite for the next run. bye.

Recap (auto):
- Run summary: brief spike at ~13:05 caused p99 tail due to an unexpected burst, steady-state otherwise acceptable.
- Tuning plan: bump concurrency to 600, enable prefix KV caching, reduce adaptive flush target to 6ms, set queue high-water to 5s with fallback after 7s.
- Deliverables: per-second CSV, p50/p95/p99 histograms, KV cache visualization, pricing update, 2-hour steady-state run.
